newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Afrox seen solid at half year.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Afrox seen solid at half year.

text.p: South African industrial gases to healthcare group African Oxygen Ltd (Afrox) is expected to post solid half year growth next week with all its main businesses moving steadily ahead, analysts said on Friday.
The firm has a market reputation for keeping its investors happy and analysts are not expecting any surprises with the interim figures to be announced next Friday.
"It has been a very reliable performer over the last few years, especially on the gases side. There should not be any surprises," said Chris Veegh, analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts polled by Reuters are looking for a rise in earnings per share on a historic basis from 31.4 cents to a range of 36.1 to 37.7 cents. The consensus figure comes in at 37.0.
The dividend is seen tracking earnings growth and rising from 11.6 cents last time to a range of 13.3 to 13.9 cents. The consensus is 13.7.
Analysts said the firm was a good defensive stock and its hallmark reliability made it a popular investment with longer-term players.
"Afrox always comes in with relatively healthy growth because they have got a lot of fat tucked away to keep their investors pleased," said one analyst who declined to be named.
"It is a good company with a good track record, but it is already priced in to the share price. A good long term share to be in, but few short-term gains," the analyst added.
Analysts said the firm was set to post further growth for the year as its Mpumalanga plant comes on line.
The scheme is the largest single project in the company's history and involves building a 1,100 tonne-a-day air separation plant and a 50 kilometre pipeline between Witbank and Middleburg.
The plant is being built to meeet the gases demands from two major customers, Columbus Stainless Steel at Middelburg and Highveld Steel and Vanadium Corp at Witbank.
